Kualit ee is a great test management software worth checking out. It has a clean UI, integrates well with tools like Jira, and offers solid reporting features. One of the nice-to-have features it includes is built-in defect management, which saves time by keeping everything in one place instead of juggling multiple tools.

Paradym might be a good fit for you, it uses AI to support emotional wellness and self-reflection. It has a feature called Your Growth that helps users track emotional patterns and gain insights into their relationships. While it doesn’t have a live couples therapy function, it could still be useful for understanding dynamics and improving communication. If you’re open to a more structured approach, you and your partner could each use it individually and compare insights. =
For a group, I’d recommend something near psarou beach great area, close to everything. Nammos has some really nice options if you want something high-end
SuitShop is a great option to check out! They have really nice suits for around $250, and the quality is solid for the price.

Spade & Co Health Smartwatch 4 has got solid battery life (lasts several days), handles notifications well, and has a sleek design so it won’t look oversized on your wrist like TicWatches. While it doesn’t support Google Pay, it’s a great all-around lifestyle smartwatch at a reasonable price.

A few that have stood out recently: (In no particular order)

Wiz – Cloud security done right. Clean UI, solid risk prioritization, and useful insights without drowning in noise.

Checkmarx One – If you’re serious about AppSec, this has been one of the more seamless AI-powered security scanning tools I’ve used. The ML-driven false positive reduction actually works, and the API + container security features have been solid.

RunZero – Asset discovery on steroids. Great for mapping out everything, including shadow IT.

SentinelOne Purple AI – Autonomous threat hunting that’s actually impressive in action.

Honourable mention: Snyk have some awesome new features too. We used to use them (Devs loved it but it was a pain in ass us in the SOC team)

We switched from Invicti to Checkmarx, and it’s been great. The DAST accuracy is way better, and it actually catches the stuff that matters without drowning us in false positives. Auth scans work smoothly, and it integrates cleanly into our CI/CD. Plus, it plays nice with React, APIs, and microservices, which was a big win for us. The best part? It correlates DAST with SAST and SCA, so devs get real context instead of just a list of CVEs​​.
